The branch imports `pruneMapToMaxSize`, caps the Microsoft Teams `teamGroupIdCache` at 500 entries after successful Graph lookups, and adds cache-cap regression coverage.

PR surface: Source +3, Tests +60. Total +63 across 2 files.

Reproducibility: yes. from source inspection: current main inserts distinct successful Teams IDs into a module-level TTL Map without a fixed maximum, and the message handler reaches that path for channel-thread replies. I did not run a live Teams tenant reproduction in this read-only review.

target.title: fix(msteams): cap team-group-id cache with pruneMapToMaxSize
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The `teamGroupIdCache` Map in `resolveTeamGroupId` had TTL-based expiry (10 min) but no size cap. A large Teams workspace with many distinct team IDs could accumulate entries faster than the TTL window, allowing unbounded growth.

## Why This Change Was Made

Added a 500-entry cap via `pruneMapToMaxSize` — the shared SDK helper already used by 11 other files. The cap is applied after each successful cache insert.

## User Impact

No change for normal usage. Memory usage bounded at ~500 entries regardless of workspace size.

## Evidence

### Vitest regression — `resolveTeamGroupId` capped at 500 through mocked Graph responses

The test mocks `fetchGraphJson` to return successful Graph responses, calls `resolveTeamGroupId` 501 times with distinct team IDs, and verifies the cache cap works:

```text
$ pnpm vitest run --project extension-msteams extensions/msteams/src/graph-thread.test.ts --reporter=verbose

 ✓ resolveTeamGroupId > caps cache at 500 entries — evicts oldest on overflow
 ... 21 passed (21)
```

The test exercises the full `resolveTeamGroupId` path:
- Fills 500 entries through successful mocked Graph lookups
- 501st entry triggers `pruneMapToMaxSize` → oldest entry (team-0) evicted
- Verifies team-0 is re-fetched from Graph (eviction proof)
- Verifies team-1 is still cached (LRU semantics)

### Lint

```text
$ npx oxlint extensions/msteams/src/graph-thread.ts
0 errors, 0 warnings
```
